relations.subject: js-udf:global-function
relations.evidence: When you call a **global** function, any partial keyspace references within the function definition are resolved against the `default:` namespace, regardless of the current [query context](../n1ql/n1ql-intro/queriesandresults.md#query-context).

relations.subject: js-udf:scoped-function
relations.evidence: When you call a **scoped** function, any partial keyspace references within the function definition are resolved against the function's bucket and scope, regardless of the current [query context](../n1ql/n1ql-intro/queriesandresults.md#query-context).

relations.subject: cloud/guides/call-user-defined-function
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - structural markdown link, and the guide's own worked example uses the statement directly
relations.evidence: To execute a user-defined function: 1. If required, [set the query context](select.md#query-context) for a scoped function, or unset the context for a global function. 2. Use the `EXECUTE FUNCTION` statement and specify the name of the function. 3. Specify the function parameters within parentheses `()`.

relations.subject: cloud/guides/call-user-defined-function

relations.evidence: The SQL++ user-defined function can be used in any SQL++ statement in exactly the same way as a standard built-in function. ... For more information and examples, see [User-Defined Functions](../n1ql/n1ql-language-reference/userfun.md).

notable_absence.finding: Unlike the other two guides in the JS UDF trio (create-javascript-library.md, create-user-defined-function.md), this page has no Query Tab UI tab at all - calling/executing a UDF is shown only as SQL++ (EXECUTE FUNCTION statement, or direct call from within a SELECT). This is a genuinely different shape from its sibling guides: creation is a UI-first task with an SQL++ alternative, but calling is SQL++-only, with the Query Tab positioned merely as the tool used to run the SQL++ statement (per the shared 'Query Tab' link in the introduction) rather than offering a separate no-code calling mechanism.
